observations.seen: A single warm key from the lower-left corner leaves a bright hotspot and lens flare at the bottom-left of the board while the upper-right board corner falls into murk. On the white board in frame 4, the hotspot blows out the solder mask and flattens the maze contrast. Small orange lamp posts at the maze corners add local warm pools but do not shape the chips.

Chips and gem pedestals cast soft, short contact shadows offset toward the upper right, which grounds them. Shadows on the off-board black pillars are dark and smeared. The shadow direction reads clearly, but there is no crisp shadow from the player courier or the enemy cones.

Faceted gems show flat per-face shading with almost no environment reflection or sparkle. Chip tops have only a faint specular rim. The board surface has no glossy solder-mask sheen picking up the room.

The board sits on a blue grid cutting mat with a pegboard wall and a wooden shelf behind it. The setting is coherent as a workbench but sparse and dim, and most of it is cropped away by the board filling the frame.
No indoor haze or volumetric light is visible. The only atmospheric cues are a slight glow halo around the corner lamps and a soft light bloom in the bottom-left corner.

The PCB reads well: green or red solder mask, copper traces, gold pads, silkscreen text ('GLINT COURIER REV 4.7'), and drilled vias. The chips are a uniform matte dark plastic with little variation. The white board variant in frame 4 looks chalky and loses trace legibility.

IC chips have modeled pins and the board has mounting holes, which is a nice level of detail. The gems are plain low-poly icosahedra, the off-board pillars are bare boxes, and the player and enemies are tiny, simple shapes that barely read at this scale.

The board fills roughly 75 to 80% of the frame, well over the 25 to 40% target. The bottom edge of the board is cropped and the top is crowded by the HUD. The player and enemies are tiny and lack focal emphasis, and decorative gems at the board edges compete for attention.

The camera is a steep, fixed, high-angle perspective with visible keystone convergence toward the top. It is not an orthographic broadcast view. The angle reads the maze adequately but compresses the far rows.

Effects present are a warm grade, a vignette, bloom on the player trail and lamps, and a lens flare at the bottom-left. Frames 3 and 4 show visible noise and banding. The bloom on the white board washes out the lower half.

Between frames 1 and 2 the player's glowing trail line moves and the score changes from 50 to 60. Otherwise the frames show nothing animated: no visible squash, particles on pickup, or enemy motion cues.

The HUD panels for score, high score, lives, shards, cache and dash are clean and readable. A top developer-style tab bar (Sentry Lab, Board Map, Courier Studio, Relay, Coil, Dash ON, Overhead) clutters the view. The 'Relay Grid GO!' banner overlaps the board, and frames 3 and 4 show no HUD at all.

nextChange.change: add the recipe row's atmosphere (fog scale, haze, shafts) at the look's intensity
